stem: A 51-year-old woman has not had a menstrual period for 12 months and is experiencing hot flashes. Her transition to menopause is best explained by which of the following changes in her ovaries?

options.label: A
options.text: Exhaustion of her remaining pool of primary oocytes
options.misconception: None; menopause is the end of the oocyte supply.
options.explanation: The number of primary oocytes in the ovaries declines from one to two million in an infant, to approximately 400,000 at puberty, to zero by the end of menopause; with no follicles left, cycles cease.

options.label: B
options.text: Failure of the pituitary to secrete FSH and LH
options.misconception: The axis is being inverted — the ovary fails, not the pituitary.
options.explanation: In menopause the depleted ovary stops responding, and FSH and LH actually rise from lost negative feedback; the initiating event is oocyte-pool exhaustion.

options.label: C
options.text: Atresia of the uterine endometrial lining
options.misconception: A downstream target is being mistaken for the cause.
options.explanation: Endometrial thinning follows the loss of ovarian estrogen; the primary change is depletion of the ovarian follicle pool.

options.label: D
options.text: Autoimmune destruction of ovarian theca cells
options.misconception: A rare pathological cause is being substituted for the physiological one.
options.explanation: Ordinary menopause is the programmed exhaustion of the finite oocyte pool formed in fetal life, not an immune attack on the ovary.

options.label: E
options.text: Conversion of remaining oocytes into corpus albicans
options.misconception: A follicle remnant is being confused with the gametes themselves.
options.explanation: The corpus albicans is the scar left by a degenerated corpus luteum; menopause occurs because the supply of primary oocytes themselves falls to zero.

context: Learning objective: explain menopausal timing. Oogonia form a finite pool of primary oocytes before birth, declining from one to two million in infancy to about 400,000 at puberty to zero by menopause; fertility peaks in the twenties and falls more rapidly after age 35 as the pool runs out.
